---
title: "annotation-gate.yml"
---

Fail a run that carries an annotation nobody allowed.

A check that emits a `::warning::` or `::notice::` on a green job tells the
reader something is wrong without stopping the merge, and agents and authors
skip it.
This gate reads the annotations of every other job in the run through the
check-runs API and fails when any `notice`, `warning` or `failure` annotation
does not match an allow pattern.

## Use

Add one job that lists every other job in `needs` and runs `if: always()`.
See `examples/annotation-gate.yml`.
Grant the job `actions: read`, `checks: read` and `contents: read`.

## Inputs

- `levels`: levels to enforce, default `notice,warning,failure`.
- `allow-patterns`: newline-separated case-insensitive regexes for tracked
  exceptions.
- `job-name`: optional extra name prefix of a job to skip.
  The gate's own job is always skipped, whatever the caller named it.

The composite action `Morrison-Lab/gha/annotation-gate@v3` also takes
`default-allow`, which replaces the allowed-for-everyone list below, and `token`.
The reusable workflow keeps the defaults.

## Allowed for everyone

- GitHub's runner-image migration notice ("The ubuntu-latest label will
  migrate to ...").
- A job's own "Process completed with exit code N" failure annotation.
  A failed job already fails the run, and the gate runs under `if: always()`,
  so this one would only repeat it.
- The forced-Node deprecation warning, until the action pins are bumped.
  It reads "Node.js N is deprecated" and then "The following actions target Node".

## Scope

Annotations from the gate's own job, and from a job that has not finished,
are not seen.
A reusable-workflow job is covered, because the jobs endpoint lists each by
its full name.
